key_insight: A parity-breaking cellular automaton built from chiral collisions and velocity rotation coarse-grains to hydrodynamics with odd viscosity, linking microscopic chirality to macroscopic odd-fluid behavior.
engineering_relevance: This provides a particle-based route to model and analyze transverse transport in active or magnetized-like fluids where conventional Navier–Stokes closures miss odd-viscous effects.
method: Start from the FHP lattice-gas automaton on a 2D triangular lattice.
Add chiral two-body collision rules to break parity symmetry.
Systematically rotate particle velocities to emulate a background magnetic field and induce odd viscosity.
evidence_signal: The authors validate the derived transport coefficients with Poiseuille-flow simulations of the chiral FHP automaton.
watch_item: As a lattice-gas model, the results may depend on coarse-graining assumptions and parameter choices when mapping to real odd-fluid materials.
paper_title: Odd fluids from chiral cellular automata
